newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: WIFO sticks to pessimistic Austria growth f'cast.
newsitem.headline: WIFO sticks to pessimistic Austria growth f'cast.

text.p: Austria's leading research institute WIFO on Friday reiterated that it expected economic growth to accelerate next year but cautioned the recovery would be fragile, pointing to slack domestic consumption.
In its quarterly economic report, WIFO stuck to earlier forecasts that GDP growth would slow to 0.7 percent this year from 1.8 percent in 1995, then rebound to 1.0 percent in 1997.
"Although economic growth should accelerate in the course of 1997, it still will not match levels seen in the middle of 1995," wrote the institute, whose figures form the basis of government policy.

Bouyant exports would contribute to the upswing next year, WIFO said, noting that exporters were benefitting from relatively stable foreign currency markets and strong demand from central and eastern Europe. The institute saw exports rising four percent this year and 5.5 percent in 1997.

Domestic consumption, in contrast, had weakened after a promising first half. WIFO predicted that private consumption would increase one percent this year and just 0.3 percent in 1997, down from 1.9 percent in 1995.
"As a result some branches of industry -- textiles, clothing, leather, construction, furniture and other consumer durables -- will see declining production," WIFO said.
It traced the drop to the effects of government savings and a higher tax burden from the beginning of 1997. Disposable income would fall 0.5 percent this year and 1.5 percent in 1997, WIFO said.

Overall sluggish economic growth meant there would be no turnaround in the employment market, with the number of jobless rising to 7.1 percent this year from 6.6 percent in 1995. In 1997 the figure would reach 7.5 percent, WIFO said.
Consumer price inflation would remain at a modest 1.7 percent this year and next, compared with 2.2 percent in 1995. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 531 12 254
